pages.contentMarkdown:
RNA Metabolism. Chapter-26. Dr. Rula Abdul Ghani.

Cover only; excluded from assessment.

pages.title: RNA roles and transcription

concepts.label: RNA functions and ribozymes
concepts.detail: RNA is presented in storage, transmission and catalytic roles; catalytic RNA is a ribozyme.

concepts.label: Transcription definition
concepts.detail: RNA sequence is complementary to one DNA strand.

pages.contentMarkdown:
- The source calls RNA the only known macromolecule with **information storage, transmission, and catalysis**.
- Catalytic RNA, a **ribozyme**, changed the definition of enzyme.
- **Transcription:** conversion of genetic information from DNA into RNA with a sequence complementary to one DNA strand.

pages.title: Three RNA roles in protein synthesis

concepts.label: mRNA, tRNA and rRNA
concepts.detail: mRNA carries codons; tRNA delivers specified amino acids; rRNA/proteins form ribosomes.

pages.contentMarkdown:
Three RNA classes have different, complementary roles in protein synthesis (translation):

| RNA | Role stated |
| --- | --- |
| mRNA | Carries DNA-copied information as three-base words called **codons** |
| tRNA | Transmits code and delivers the specified amino acid |
| rRNA | Associates with proteins to form **ribosomes**, protein-synthesizing machines |

pages.title: Transcription versus replication

concepts.label: Transcription/replication comparison
concepts.detail: Shared template-driven 5-prime to 3-prime synthesis and PPi hydrolysis; transcription needs no primer and covers a limited DNA segment.

pages.contentMarkdown:
The source comparison lists:

1. Similar chemical reaction/mechanism: **PPi hydrolysis** drives synthesis forward.
2. Stages: initiation, elongation, termination.
3. Template needed.
4. Synthesis polarity **5' to 3'**.
5. Transcription requires **no primer**.
6. Transcription covers a **limited DNA segment**.
7. Transcription has **no 3' to 5' proofreading activity** and cannot excise mismatched nucleotides, as stated.

pages.title: Transcription requirements

concepts.label: Transcription requirements
concepts.detail: RNA polymerase uses a 3-prime to 5-prime template, ATP/GTP/CTP/UTP and stated metal ions without primer.

pages.contentMarkdown:
1. **RNA polymerase**.
2. **DNA template**, the 3' to 5' strand.
3. **No primer required**.
4. Nucleoside triphosphates **ATP, GTP, CTP, UTP**.
5. Synthesis **5' to 3'**.
6. **Mg2+ and Zn2+**.

pages.title: Overall RNA-synthesis reaction

concepts.label: RNA polymerization reaction
concepts.detail: Adding NTP extends RNA by one NMP and releases PPi.

pages.contentMarkdown:
**(NMP)n + NTP -> (NMP)n+1 + PPi**

The initial polymer is labeled **RNA**, the product **lengthened RNA**.

pages.title: DNA-dependent synthesis of RNA

concepts.label: RNA extension chemistry
concepts.detail: Incoming rNTP joins the 3-prime OH; base pairing and geometry guide selection.

concepts.label: Transcription bubble
concepts.detail: An 8-bp RNA-DNA hybrid lies within the bubble; unwinding ahead and rewinding behind accompany movement.

pages.visualNotes: All bubble/strand labels and 3-prime-OH annotation reviewed.
pages.contentMarkdown:
RNA polymerase adds ribonucleotide units to the **3'-hydroxyl end**, building RNA **5' to 3'**.

- Nucleotides are selected by Watson-Crick pairing; base-pair geometry contributes to selection.
- The 3' OH at the active site acts as nucleophile attacking the phosphate of incoming **rNTP**.
- Figure labels: **transcription bubble**, **nontemplate strand**, **template strand**, **RNA polymerase**, **active site**, **RNA-DNA hybrid, 8 bp**, emerging RNA 5' end.
- In the depicted left-to-right transcription direction, DNA **unwinds ahead** at right and **rewinds behind** at left.

pages.title: Stages of transcription

concepts.label: Initiation, elongation, termination
concepts.detail: Promoter initiation precedes elongation with a transient 8-bp hybrid; termination ends transcription.

concepts.label: RNA elongation rate
concepts.detail: The source gives 50-90 nucleotides/s.
concepts.rationale: Supporting detail or illustration; no exam probability implied.

pages.contentMarkdown:
- **Initiation:** starts at a promoter; RNA polymerase binds specific DNA sequences.
- **Elongation:** growing RNA temporarily pairs with the template as a short **8 bp RNA-DNA hybrid**; hybrid peels off and the DNA duplex reforms. Rate: **50-90 nucleotides/s**.
- **Termination:** named as the third stage; mechanisms follow on later pages.

pages.title: Transcription and DNA supercoiling

concepts.label: Transcriptional supercoiling
concepts.detail: Movement creates negative supercoils behind and positive ahead; topoisomerase relieves them.

concepts.label: Bubble dimensions
concepts.detail: The slide labels 17 bp unwound and an 8-bp hybrid.
concepts.rationale: Supporting detail or illustration; no exam probability implied.

pages.visualNotes: Supercoil signs and spatial relationships checked.
pages.contentMarkdown:
Because DNA is helical, transcription-bubble movement requires strand rotation, causing supercoiling in vitro and in vivo; **topoisomerase** relieves it.

The left-to-right figure depicts **negative supercoils behind** the transcription complex and **positive supercoils ahead**, labels emerging RNA 5' end, and annotates **17 bp unwound, 8 bp DNA-RNA hybrid**.

pages.title: Coding and template strands

concepts.label: Coding versus template strand
concepts.detail: RNA matches the coding strand except U/T and is complementary to the template.

pages.visualNotes: All sequences transcribed from image; 13 bases each.
pages.contentMarkdown:
The **coding/nontemplate strand** has the transcript sequence except that RNA uses **U instead of T**.

| Molecule | Sequence and orientation in source |
| --- | --- |
| DNA nontemplate (coding) | 5'-CGCTATAGCGTTT-3' |
| DNA template | 3'-GCGATATCGCAAA-5' |
| RNA transcript | 5'-CGCUAUAGCGUUU-3' |

pages.title: E. coli DNA-dependent RNA polymerase

concepts.label: Core and sigma
concepts.detail: E. coli RNA polymerase core is alpha2/beta/beta-prime/omega; transient sigma directs specific DNA recognition.

concepts.label: RNA polymerase error rate
concepts.detail: The source literally prints one error/104-105; exponent formatting is unresolved and exact numerical frequency is blocked.
concepts.rationale: Supporting detail or illustration; no exam probability implied.

uncertainties.description: Source literally prints one error/104-105 with 4 and 5 on the baseline in the rendered slide and text layer. Do not silently convert to 10^4-10^5; exact numerical error-frequency assessment is blocked until formatting is clarified.

pages.contentMarkdown:
- Large complex: **five core subunits** plus a sixth **sigma** subunit.
- Sigma binds the core transiently and directs it to specific DNA-binding sequences.
- Source states no 3' to 5' exonuclease proofreading and **one error/104-105** (literal source formatting; exponent meaning unresolved).
- Diagram: core **alpha, alpha, beta, beta-prime, omega** labeled **constant**; **sigma** labeled **variable**.

pages.title: Transcription-initiation coordinates

concepts.label: Upstream, downstream and +1
concepts.detail: +1 is the start; downstream is positive and upstream negative.

concepts.label: Promoter-bound regulators
concepts.detail: RNA polymerase, activators and repressors act at promoters.

pages.contentMarkdown:
- Transcription-initiation/start site is **+1**.
- **Downstream**, in the transcription direction, receives positive numbers.
- **Upstream**, opposite to transcription, receives negative numbers.
- RNA polymerase, activators and repressors interact with promoter DNA to regulate initiation.

pages.title: Typical gene structure

concepts.label: Promoter and coding region
concepts.detail: Diagram places promoter upstream of +1 and coding region downstream.

pages.contentMarkdown: Schematic: **promoter** precedes the **coding region**. The **+1** boundary marks transcription start; **downstream** and transcription arrows point through the coding region to the right.

pages.title: E. coli promoter sequences

concepts.label: E. coli promoter recognition
concepts.detail: -10 TATAAT and -35 TTGACA are recognition sequences; UP element may occur at -40 to -60.

concepts.label: Promoter spacer labels
concepts.detail: Diagram marks N17 and N6 spacers.
concepts.rationale: Supporting detail or illustration; no exam probability implied.

pages.visualNotes: Image enlarged; core hexamers, positions and spacer lengths readable.

uncertainties.description: Exact UP-element consensus cannot be transcribed confidently from tightly stacked A/T alternatives. Preserve source image via PDF p14; block exact-base sequence questions for this UP element.

pages.contentMarkdown:
- **-10 region:** 5'-**TATAAT**-3'.
- **-35 region:** 5'-**TTGACA**-3'.
- **UP element:** upstream promoter region between **-40 and -60**, not present in all bacteria.
- Mutations at -10 or -35 affect polymerase-binding efficiency and transcription initiation.
- The image labels **consensus sequence** (annotated as common), UP element, -35 region, spacer, -10 region, spacer, RNA start **+1**.
- Between the -35 and -10 consensus hexamers the spacer is **N17**; the following spacer before +1 is **N6**. An N precedes TTGACA.
- The UP consensus image contains many A/T positions and Ns with stacked alternatives; its exact linear representation is unresolved below.

pages.title: Bacterial initiation and promoter clearance

concepts.label: Closed/open complexes and clearance
concepts.detail: Promoter binding precedes DNA opening, initiation and promoter clearance; sigma dissociates as elongation begins.

pages.visualNotes: All initiation panels and sigma-release arrow reviewed.
pages.contentMarkdown:
1. **Binding:** RNA polymerase binds promoter, forming a **closed complex** with intact DNA, then an **open complex** with DNA intact but unwound at **-10**, as worded.
2. **Initiation:** transcription begins; complex moves away from promoter (**promoter clearance**).
3. **Elongation:** **sigma dissociates** and polymerase leaves the promoter.

The diagram follows binding -> closed complex -> open complex -> initiation of transcription -> promoter clearance, showing sigma leaving and RNA emerging. UP, -35, -10 and +1 labels locate binding.

pages.title: Transcription termination overview

concepts.label: Termination classes
concepts.detail: Bacterial termination may require Rho; eukaryotic mechanisms differ by polymerase.

pages.contentMarkdown:
- Several mechanisms regulate termination in bacteria and eukaryotes.
- Bacteria have two principal mechanisms involving RNA polymerase; one additionally requires **Rho**.
- Eukaryotic termination mechanisms differ among the **three RNA polymerases**.

pages.title: Factor-independent and Rho-dependent termination

concepts.label: Rho-dependent termination
concepts.detail: Rho moves 5-prime to 3-prime on mRNA and uses ATP-dependent helicase activity to disrupt RNA-DNA hybrid.

concepts.label: Factor-independent termination
concepts.detail: Source associates a GC-rich transcript and weak A-U region with transcription-bubble collapse.

pages.visualNotes: Text checked alongside hairpin diagrams on pp18-19.

uncertainties.description: P17 explains slowing as GC pairs making the template hard to unwind, while pp18-19 depict a transcript hairpin. Preserve both; block the precise causal unwinding explanation rather than silently repairing it.

pages.contentMarkdown:
**Factor independent:**

- A **GC-rich transcript segment** is stated to make the template hard to unwind and slow RNA polymerase.
- Weak **A=U bonds** cause further weakening/dissociation, collapsing the transcription bubble.

**Rho (rho) factor dependent:**

- Rho loads at specific mRNA-binding sites and moves **5' to 3'** toward the transcription complex.
- It proceeds along mRNA and probably outraces/catches up to RNA polymerase, as worded.
- Its **ATP-dependent helicase activity** disrupts the RNA-DNA hybrid.
- Termination completes with release of Rho and RNA polymerase from nucleic acids.

concepts.label: Terminator hairpin recognition

pages.title: Hairpin-associated termination diagram

concepts.label: Pause, isomerize, terminate
concepts.detail: The diagram associates RNA hairpin formation with pausing/isomerization before termination.

pages.contentMarkdown:
The three-stage figure labels **Pause -> Isomerize -> Terminate**.

concepts.label: RNA polymerases I, II and III
concepts.detail: I transcribes rRNA genes, II mRNA genes, III tRNAs, as listed.

concepts.label: Multimeric eukaryotic polymerases

concepts.rationale: Supporting detail or illustration; no exam probability implied.

pages.contentMarkdown:
| Polymerase | Transcripts stated |
| --- | --- |
| RNA polymerase I | rRNA genes |
| RNA polymerase II | Genes encoding mRNAs |
| RNA polymerase III | tRNAs |

All three are **multimeric enzymes with more than 10 subunits**. These are the examples stated; the slide does not establish that each list is exhaustive.

pages.title: Eukaryotic promoters

concepts.label: TATA and Inr
concepts.detail: Eukaryotic TATAAA lies near -30; initiation/unwinding is associated with Inr near +1.

concepts.label: Consensus symbols
concepts.detail: N represents any nucleotide and Y a pyrimidine.
concepts.rationale: Supporting detail or illustration; no exam probability implied.

pages.visualNotes: Promoter motif and stacked T/A alternative read visually.
pages.contentMarkdown:
- DNA unwinds at the **Initiator (Inr)** sequence.
- **TATA box:** consensus **TATAAA**, near **-30**.
- Figure runs 5' to 3' through various regulatory sequences, TATA box at -30, and **Inr** near **+1**.
- The Inr motif is drawn **YYAN(T/A)YY**, with the T/A alternative stacked.

pages.title: Transcription at RNA polymerase II promoters

concepts.label: RNA pol II initiation-complex assembly
concepts.detail: TBP-associated factors assemble polymerase II and form closed/open complexes.

concepts.label: TFIIH helicase and kinase
concepts.detail: TFIIH is labeled for DNA opening and RNA pol II phosphorylation.

concepts.label: Polymerase II recycling
concepts.detail: After termination, polymerase II is released, dephosphorylated and reused.

pages.visualNotes: Every factor label, phosphorylation symbol and recycling arrow reviewed.
pages.contentMarkdown:
The figure follows **assembly, initiation, elongation, termination**, then polymerase recycling.

1. DNA shows **TATA at -30** and **Inr at +1**.
2. Assembly labels, in order shown: **TBP (or TFIID and/or TFIIA)**; **TFIIB**; **TFIIF-RNA polymerase II**; **TFIIE**; **TFIIH**.
3. A **closed complex** contains TFIID/TFIIA/TFIIB/TBP, TFIIF, TFIIE, TFIIH and RNA polymerase II. An annotation says **stabilize**.
4. **TFIIH helicase** annotation accompanies DNA unwinding to form the **open complex**.
5. **TFIIH kinase activity** phosphorylates RNA polymerase II; initiation and release of the elongation complex follow. The emerging polymerase tail bears phosphate symbols.
6. **TFIIH and TFIIE** are shown leaving. **Elongation factors** join; elongation is annotated **after the first 60-70 nucleotides**.
7. Termination releases RNA; RNA polymerase II is released and dephosphorylated, then recycled for another cycle.

The figure retains some initiation factors at the promoter rather than showing every protein traveling with polymerase.

concepts.label: Transcription-factor functions
concepts.detail: Table links TBP/TFIIA/TFIIB/TFIID/TFIIE/TFIIF/TFIIH to promoter assembly, regulation and repair.

concepts.label: Elongation-factor role
concepts.detail: ELL, P-TEFb, SII and Elongin suppress polymerase II-TFIIF pausing/arrest.

concepts.label: Factor subunits and Mr
concepts.detail: Full source table masses, subunit counts and ELL footnote retained.

pages.visualNotes: Image enlarged; complete table and both footnotes transcribed.

pages.contentMarkdown:
**Table 26-1. Proteins Required for Transcription at the RNA Polymerase II Promoters of Eukaryotes** (screenshot reconstructed). The table labels masses **Subunit Mr**; no additional unit is added here.

| Initiation factor | Subunits | Subunit Mr | Function in table |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| RNA polymerase II | 12 | 10,000-220,000 | Catalyzes RNA synthesis |
| TBP (TATA-binding protein) | 1 | 38,000 | Specifically recognizes TATA box |
| TFIIA | 3 | 12,000, 19,000, 35,000 | Stabilizes binding of TFIIB and TBP to promoter |
| TFIIB | 1 | 35,000 | Binds TBP; recruits RNA polymerase-TFIIF complex |
| TFIID | 12 | 15,000-250,000 | Interacts with positive and negative regulatory proteins |
| TFIIE | 2 | 34,000, 57,000 | Recruits TFIIH; ATPase and helicase activities, as printed |
| TFIIF | 2 | 30,000, 74,000 | Binds tightly to RNA polymerase II; binds TFIIB and prevents polymerase binding to nonspecific DNA sequences |
| TFIIH | 12 | 35,000-89,000 | Unwinds DNA at promoter; phosphorylates RNA polymerase; recruits nucleotide-excision repair complex |

A red annotation states **More than 30 polypeptide**.

| Elongation factor | Subunits | Subunit Mr |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| ELL | 1 | 80,000 |
| P-TEFb | 2 | 43,000, 124,000 |
| SII (TFIIS) | 1 | 38,000 |
| Elongin (SIII) | 3 | 15,000, 18,000, 110,000 |

Footnotes:

- All elongation factors suppress pausing/arrest of transcription by the RNA polymerase II-TFIIF complex.
- ELL derives from **eleven-nineteen lysine-rich leukemia**. The ELL gene is a site of chromosomal-recombination events frequently associated with **acute myeloid leukemia**.

All numerical inventory details are preserved as supporting source content; assessment priority should favor clearly explained functional relationships.

pages.title: TFIIH and transcription-associated repair

concepts.label: TFIIH repair recruitment
concepts.detail: At an RNA pol II-blocking lesion, TFIIH interacts with damage and recruits NER.

pages.contentMarkdown:
When **RNA polymerase II halts at a DNA lesion**, **TFIIH**, beyond its role in closed-complex formation:

pages.title: Transcription inhibition

concepts.label: Actinomycin versus rifampicin
concepts.detail: Actinomycin inhibits elongation; rifampicin inhibits promoter clearance.

concepts.label: Intercalation
concepts.detail: Insertion between successive G-C base pairs deforms DNA and impedes RNA polymerase.

concepts.label: Illustrated inhibitor structures
concepts.detail: Actinomycin D and Acridine structures are shown.
concepts.rationale: Supporting detail or illustration; no exam probability implied.

uncertainties.description: Rifampicin appears under a broad intercalating-agents heading, but only promoter-clearance inhibition is explicitly assigned to it. Do not infer or score a rifampicin intercalation mechanism from layout.

pages.contentMarkdown:
The heading is **Intercalating agents inhibit RNA polymerase**.

- Intercalation inserts an agent between successive **G-C base pairs** in double-helical DNA, deforming DNA and preventing polymerase movement along the template.
- **Actinomycin** inhibits **elongation**.
- **Rifampicin** inhibits **promoter clearance**.

The chemical figures are labeled **Actinomycin D** and **Acridine**. Actinomycin D depicts a central multiring chromophore with two peptide-ring arms; labels include **Sar, L-Pro, L-meVal, D-Val, L-Thr**, carbonyl/O/N groups, NH2 and CH3. Acridine is shown as three fused rings with a nitrogen-bearing central ring and N-H/positive-charge symbols.

Rifampicin's inhibitory stage is stated separately; the slide does not explicitly assign it an intercalation mechanism.

pages.title: After the primary transcript

concepts.label: Primary-transcript fates
concepts.detail: The source contrasts direct prokaryotic translation with eukaryotic modification/export/translation.

pages.contentMarkdown:
- **Prokaryotes:** RNA translated directly into protein.
- **Eukaryotes:** RNA modified, exported to cytoplasm, then translated.

These are the primary-transcript comparisons made in the slide; no additional processing exceptions are imported.

pages.title: Post-transcriptional processing in eukaryotes

concepts.label: Eukaryotic mRNA processing
concepts.detail: Nuclear splicing, capping and polyadenylation precede cytoplasmic translation.

pages.contentMarkdown:
- Genes are transcribed in the **nucleus** to RNA.
- In the nucleus, mRNA is **spliced**, **5'-capped**, and **3'-polyadenylated**.
- mRNA is transported to the **cytoplasm for translation**.

pages.title: Three eukaryotic mRNA modifications

concepts.label: Capping, splicing and polyadenylation
concepts.detail: Cap at 5-prime; introns removed/exons joined; 3-prime cleavage and poly(A) addition.

concepts.label: Alternative splicing
concepts.detail: Some transcripts can be spliced in multiple ways with regulatory significance.

concepts.label: Poly(A) tail length
concepts.detail: The source gives 80-250 A residues.
concepts.rationale: Supporting detail or illustration; no exam probability implied.

concepts.label: Processing and phosphorylated CTD
concepts.detail: Processing is associated with phosphorylated CTD and RNA pol II.

pages.contentMarkdown:
1. **Capping:** modified **5' cap** residue is added at the 5' end before transcription ends.
2. **Splicing:** introns are removed and exons joined. **Alternative splicing** allows some transcripts to be spliced in more than one way and has regulatory significance.
3. **Polyadenylation:** the 3' end is cleaved and **80-250 A residues** are added as a **poly(A) tail**.

The source states these modifications work together with **phosphorylated CTD and RNA polymerase II**. The list enumerates modification types and does not establish a unique chronological order for all three processes.

pages.title: Primary transcript to mature mRNA diagram

concepts.label: Primary-to-mature transcript diagram
concepts.detail: Image links capped exon/intron-containing primary RNA to mature mRNA with retained exons and poly(A) tail.

pages.visualNotes: Image-only teaching page fully reviewed, including all labels and dashed exon guides.
pages.contentMarkdown:
The diagram explicitly connects these stages:

1. **Transcription and 5' capping:** RNA polymerase moves along DNA, leaving emerging RNA labeled **5' cap**, **exon** and **intron**.
2. **Completion of primary transcript:** a **primary transcript** contains the cap, alternating exon/intron segments, and a **noncoding end sequence** toward the **3'** end.
3. **Cleavage, polyadenylation, and splicing:** introns loop out and are removed; dashed guides show retained exon segments joining, while end cleavage and poly(A) addition are grouped with splicing.
4. **Mature mRNA:** joined exon segments retain the **5' cap**, noncoding end segment and **AAA(A)n** at the **3'** end.

These grouped operations do not justify requiring an arbitrary unique order among cleavage, polyadenylation and individual splicing events.
